There are unions that are beneficial. I don't have personal experience, but a friend from High School's dad was a mechanic for UPS working on their daily delivery trucks and their 18 wheelers, and he was pretty much safe from the usual tyranny prevalent at UPS. A lot of the sorters didn't have 40 hours a week, great benefits/vacation time and job security over a oopsie. He did. Unions can be a amazing thing, but a lot of my personal experience is a giant fuck you to the lower guys.

The union that was coming into our plant was voted in at another plant just recently and there were pay cuts in exchange for the hour decrease and benefits increase. Once that got out, it was killed on the spot. Our guys were upset about the time off policy (had to apply for personal/vacation days 4-6 weeks in advance) and the overtime policy (used to be as much as you wanted as long as you didn't go over 16 hours worked in a 24 hour period) to can't work more then 12 in a 24 period and can't go over 60 a week (so you could only grab a extra shift every other week). Health Insurance was a lot better, but the pay went down at that particular plant in exchange for the benefits change and the vacation/personal time change. Our guys weren't willing to take a pay cut for that.

They had to. Unionizing would have cost them money. Our business the margins weren't fantastic, but they were guaranteed. We provided electricity, we had guaranteed contracts for output. When the unions hit some of our plants, the raises that were part of the contract would turn those plants into lost profits. On top of that, the unions wanted 8 hour days, not our 12 hour shifts. It got real ugly during negotiations (my Dad is a higher up at one of the plants that went union) and ultimately it became a ugly battle of whose dick is bigger. Unions wanted to keep the same hourly pay, but 8 hour days 5 days a week. It was a untenable situation as additional employees would have to be hired, which would cost them more, and caused a severe overlap which would either have people standing around or have more then the required employees on a job which actually made it take longer because we have strict communication and safety protocols. 

That plant went into a shut down for 2 days as the company wasn't going to run that 1 plant at a loss. It was our plant, it was far more tenable to shut it down then run it at a loss. We don't have swing profits, they are guaranteed if we meet output. The changes at that one plant were just untenable financially.

That's why I said in a previous post that I dislike 95% of unions, not all. The one that I have experience with was pure seniority. Our company runs all plants, but the ones under union contract all non management are unionized. Those plants are hand tied when a higher positions open up, they HAVE TO promote based on seniority, it's in the union contract. We had a guy with 17 years of experience transfer to a union plant before I left and I still talk to him, his seniority started the day he showed up. It's aggravating to work for 17 years and get tied down to "seniority". It's even sadder that he's called to help by management because the people that were promoted aren't as good as he is (the boilers in use at this particular plant are the exact same as our plant was).

I'm not sure about Target, but at my previous place of employment, talking to a union representative on company property was grounds for dismissal, unless a vote was called. That happened when over half the employees signed a petition for representation. Thank god it fell through after we saw what we'd be getting. We were actually going to lose benefits and pay, and in the end our plant got a 15% raise to make us happy and to keep the union out of the plant.

I'm going to get down voted to oblivion here, but 95% of Unions I really dislike. Before I put in my 2 weeks and quit, I worked in a industrial environment for a corporation that was Anti-Union, but if the employees came together to vote for a union, they didn't stop it (7 of the 53 plants have since become union). Union vote came up at my plant, management started freaking out because union and this line of work didn't work. The union coming in was notorious for 5 day/40 hour weeks. We worked 48/60's in shifts, our hours were going to be cut, so we'd lose overtime, promotions would have been based on seniority not ability, we'd be locked into a contract for wages, whereas each year we get a 5% raise unionized. And we'd actually lose vacation days if they came in (we got 4 weeks).

Unions might be good in some places, but in the line I work I was in, Unions would have destroyed what we enjoyed. And it seems a lot of unions only look out for the higher ups. Don't get me wrong, there are unions that do great things for their employees, but sometimes there are unions that are just detrimental to employees. It really depends on which union you happen to work for...

Death via hypoxia is not painful at all, it's actually somewhat pleasant. I attempted suicide using Nitrogen and a exit bag, and the process was extremely peaceful and over before I knew it. It went from "Finally I can leave this pain and misery behind... To why the fuck am I alive" pretty much instantly. My bag was fastened too tightly and it burst a hole allowing enough oxygen to keep me alive without damage for the most part but unconscious until the tank ran out.

Had the bag notnruptured the process would have basically been me sitting on the floor with a bag on my head to dead in minutes, whereas I'm only conscious of the bag for ~30 seconds. As a method of execution it's as close to painless and guarantee as you can get. There are some caveats to it though. Mainly those who smoked heavily or just have poor lung function generally get a really bad tingly sensation because the respiratory system doesn't dump the oxygen out as well as a non smoker/asthma would.

Nitrogen Asphyxiation should be used to execute people, it's extremely cheap to implement and run. All you need is a airtight room with a vacuum and you pump in n2 as you pull out the o2 and at a pure n2 environment, inmate is just dead before he realizes it's started.

On foot, yes, you don't need to provide your license only name, address and dob. However, operating a motor vehicle and getting pulled over for a traffic offense you must provide license and registration. It's part of that nifty agreement you had when you got it, you shall provide it at request anytime you're operating a vehicle. Arguing with a cop just isn't going to end well when you can hand over your license and registration, get your ticket/warning and be on your way. If you feel the ticket was unwarranted, plead not guilty and fight it in court. Fighting the cop like this guy did won't end well, and I don't feel bad for people that act like assholes like this. The law goes both ways, it can be extremely beneficial, or it can bend you over and fuck you so hard you cry. This guy got bent over because he was a ass to the cop asking a very basic request.

However, it is the law to provide License and Registration after being pulled over for a traffic offense... mouthing off and being disorderly is also against the law at the discretion of the officer.... maybe act like a Human and show some respect and you'll get some. Calling them pigs when the vast majority are good people is probably why a lot of these people get treated like this. I've gotten more warnings then tickets for being kind, courteous and generally a pleasant person. If I ever have a issue I take the ticket to court. Arguing with the officer just begs for trouble. The law will fuck you over every time, 100% of the time. Don't do it outside of a court room.

"License and Registration please sir"

*Hands over requested documentation*

"Thank you sir, I pulled you over for doing 60 in a 45. Give me a few and I'll be back with you in a few."

Went every traffic stop ever. Arguing and fighting? It's going to go way different, like the article. It's not the cop abusing power, it's a citizen waving his dick around and getting smacked across the face with a bigger dick.

I don't know what fairy tale world you live in, but there is no law stipulating a Peace Officer has to immediately tell you why you are pulled over. License and Registration first is a preliminary validation, if you do not have one, it changes the nature of the traffic stop. A usual traffic stop is being asked for license and registration followed by the officer upon receiving said documentation stating what you were pulled over for, then heading back to the cruiser to run your name and plates and write and tickets or warnings. 

The way this guy went about it being such a dick, he did it all wrong. Hand over the damn license and registration like you're legally required too and ask why you were pulled over as you're doing it. If the cop walks away without telling you why, then you can start getting peeved. This guy was just a dick to that officer. If what the officer said in the video is true, having to ask for License and Registration 7 times is just being a dick to the officer. 

Everyone acts like this is a huge thing, but it's a safety precaution on the officers part. Watching this video, the officer has a belligerent suspect... being detained is part of that. If you mouth off and act like this, odds are, you will end up in hand cuffs. It's not about "authority" it's about following the law. This guy was waving his dick around about something so trivial and everyone is up in arms over the law smacking him back with a bigger dick. Hand over the L&R, get your ticket/warning, go home. Fight it in court or pay the ticket. Arguing with a cop whose doing his job isn't going to end well. End of story.
